title: When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill
summary: The method replaces a monolithic, synchronously-loaded remote KV cache tier (LMCache with a single Valkey store) with a rank-sharded store, per-rank server partitioning, asynchronous loading, and client bug fixes. It costs additional serving infrastructure (one cache server instance per context-parallel rank), integration complexity with context parallelism, and client-side engineering; the model itself is unchanged so quality is unaffected. It can fail when the remote tier delivers less than the breakeven bandwidth (2.53 GB/s here), when prompts are shorter than roughly 17k tokens (where recompute always wins due to a ~0.33 s fixed per-hit cost), or when synchronous loading turns hit-heavy traffic into an unstable queue with idle GPUs.
rationale: The techniques target multi-node B300-scale disaggregated serving with context parallelism, but the cost model (hit pays off only above bandwidth B* and above a minimum prompt length) and the async-loading lesson are worth tracking for any future remote KV cache deployment.
technique: Sharded asynchronous remote KV cache tier

claims.statement: The method replaces a monolithic, synchronously-loaded remote KV cache tier (LMCache with a single Valkey store) with a rank-sharded store, per-rank server partitioning, asynchronous loading, and client bug fixes. It costs additional serving infrastructure (one cache server instance per context-parallel rank), integration complexity with context parallelism, and client-side engineering; the model itself is unchanged so quality is unaffected. It can fail when the remote tier delivers less than the breakeven bandwidth (2.53 GB/s here), when prompts are shorter than roughly 17k tokens (where recompute always wins due to a ~0.33 s fixed per-hit cost), or when synchronous loading turns hit-heavy traffic into an unstable queue with idle GPUs.

Sharded MLA KV store raises prefill throughput by 14%, and by 34% with an upstream kernel fix; on a hit-heavy stream p99 falls from 83.32 s to 0.67 s with 98.5% of prompt tokens served remotely; per-rank partitioning raises GET bandwidth 6.3x to 10.76 GB/s.
